title: Sisters sue Española over traffic stop they say was illegal

reports.title: Sisters sue Española over traffic stop they say was illegal

summary:
Two sisters from Rio Arriba County have sued Española, saying police stopped them illegally on July 23. Their car passed through an intersection with a Flock Safety camera, and the camera wrongly flagged its plate as stolen from Rio Rancho. The plate differed by one digit, ending in 2 but read as 7. Jaclynn Gonzales, 21, owned the car, and her 12-year-old sister, identified as DD, was a passenger. Officers pulled them over on Calle Duran, handcuffed both and put them in separate police cars before learning of the error, according to separate lawsuits filed Jan. 3 in state District Court.

The sisters seek unspecified damages and compensation for personal injuries, including emotional distress and restricted movement. Their attorney, Sheri Raphaelson, filed a similar April lawsuit for Adam Pacheco, who was 17 when state police stopped him based on faulty camera information and made him kneel in the road. The city of Española, Police Chief Mizel A. Garcia and Flock Safety did not respond to requests for comment. No next steps are reported.
